meta.title: Voltaire's answer to a broken world: tend your garden
meta.search_phrase: we must cultivate our garden meaning

beats.text: In Candide, Voltaire mocks a tutor who insists this is the best of all possible worlds.
Then he buries that cheerful idea under war, earthquake, disease, and betrayal.
Candide roams the earth chasing grand answers to why there is so much suffering.
He finds none. The big questions stay unanswered. The cosmos offers no tidy reason.
At the end he meets an old farmer who ignores all of it and simply works his small plot of land.
And Candide finally understands. "We must cultivate our garden."
Stop waiting for the world to make sense. Tend what is in front of you, and do it well.
